It does not check the test count or test identities, so a zero-test successful unittest result satisfies that individual decision. This is an analysis of the branch condition; no zero-test run of this workflow is asserted.
findings.boundary: The subsequent ten mutant invocations have separate one-test checks; this finding alone does not establish that the whole mutation runner accepted a zero-test execution or that any recorded run was false.

findings.observation: The runner invokes unittest discovery with -B -S; the tests import the subject through the normal module loader. -B prevents bytecode writes but does not disable reads of pre-existing valid bytecode. Mutant tests are copied into fresh temporary directories, but the workflow does not expressly isolate PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX.
findings.boundary: No poisoned cache or stale bytecode is shown to have existed in the hosted run. The normal loader creates a source-attribution limitation; actual adverse controls are needed.

This avoids attributing the final driver replay-tool load to the normal import mechanism above.
